text:
The degree of idealization also predicts the degree of demonization for me. I don’t mean this as a clinical diagnosis, but I use it almost diagnostically in my own life. If a woman says, “You’re such a great guy. Of course you have flaws like anyone, but I love you,” that sounds healthy. If she says, “You’re perfect. I can’t find any flaw,” I’m already running.

When the BPD splitting happens, and someone flips from seeing you as all good to seeing you as all bad, private hatred can replace worship. Then come public accusations, rewriting the whole past and treating every flaw as proof that the person was fake all along. Sometimes the woman who thought I was perfect later accuses me of thinking I’m perfect.
reader: Someone being adored early in a relationship, deciding whether that is love or a warning sign.
